body: Chan, Lakonishok and Sougiannis, 'The Stock Market Valuation of Research and Development Expenditures' (Journal of Finance 56(6), 2001; ~1,900 citations), US 1975-1995: on average R&D-intensive firms earn normal returns, so the market does not systematically undervalue R&D. However, firms with high R&D relative to market value (R&D-intensive and out of favour, typically after poor past returns) earn large excess returns, and R&D intensity is associated with higher return volatility. Eberhart, Maxwell and Siddique, 'An Examination of Long-Term Abnormal Stock Returns and Operating Performance Following R&D Increases' (Journal of Finance 59(2), 2004; ~740 Crossref citations): firms that unexpectedly and significantly raise R&D see positive long-run abnormal stock returns and better operating performance over five years, so the market underreacts to R&D investment. Lev and Srivastava, 'Explaining the Recent Failure of Value Investing' (Critical Finance Review 2022): book value ignores expensed intangibles, so 'cheap' P/B portfolios are full of weak old-economy firms and 'expensive' ones hold intangible-rich winners. Adjusting book value for capitalised R&D and SG&A recovers part of the value premium. Replicated: CLS and Eberhart broadly confirmed; Lev-Srivastava is plausible but debated (Arnott et al. add other causes). Use for us: for Indian pharma, specialty chemicals, IT and consumer brands, capitalise R&D and brand spend mentally before calling a stock expensive. Treat a deliberate R&D step-up during a weak year (a cheap stock with rising R&D) as a potential positive, the opposite of the capitalisation red flag. Check the expense line and pipeline, not the capitalised asset.

data.cls: high R&D/MV firms earn excess returns; average R&D firms do not
data.eberhart: positive 5-year abnormal returns after R&D increases

title: R&D and intangibles are mispriced: R&D-intensive cheap stocks outperform (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis 2001), R&D increases drift up (Eberhart et al. 2004), and intangibles broke P/B value (Lev-Srivastava 2022)
